jobs.why: GSAP ScrollTrigger pins and scrubs each chapter. Lenis smooths the scroll so it feels slow and heavy.

alternatives.when: the story is a video that plays as you scroll
the page is a 3D world you move through
I'm already in React and only need a scroll progress value

jobs.why: three.js written with React Three Fiber and drei. I own the scene, so it can react to scroll and the cursor.

alternatives.when: a designer builds the scene by hand and it rarely changes
I need a ready piece, like an orb or a globe, not a whole scene
the scene needs bloom, grain or a pixel pass on top
it behaves like a small game and wants a visual editor
the project is Svelte, not React

jobs.why: OGL when I write the shader in code. Unicorn Studio when I want to tune it by eye in an editor and embed it. A shader is a small program the graphics card runs for every pixel.

alternatives.when: all I need is a soft moving gradient
I want a ready React component with props, like grain or dither
I want sliders to tune a shader live while I build it
I've paid for it and need a premium background fast

jobs.why: The browser's own View Transition API. It animates from the old page to the new one with a few lines of CSS.

alternatives.when: one element should morph into its place on the next page (GSAP Flip)
the site is plain HTML pages, not a single-page app
I'm animating layout changes inside a React page

jobs.why: GSAP SplitText cuts a line into words or letters, then a timeline moves them in order.

alternatives.when: I want a ready text effect to paste in and restyle
the page has no React and I want something small
the text is part of a React component's state

jobs.job: I want buttons and small things to feel alive
jobs.why: Motion gives springs, hover and press states to React components. Micro-interactions are the small responses to a tap or a hover.

alternatives.when: I need to pick or draw the exact curve first
a designer animated it by hand in After Effects or Lottie
I want to try the idea visually before I code it
the page has no React

jobs.why: One consistent line set, tree-shaken so only the icons I use ship.

alternatives.when: the icon has to animate, like a loader or a success tick

jobs.note: I don't have a live piece for icons yet.

jobs.job: I want a 3D model or a hero image
jobs.why: Higgsfield makes the still first. I approve it, then turn it into a 3D model (a GLB file) or a short loop.

alternatives.when: I want the object rebuilt in code, so every part can animate
a free real model, texture or lighting file already exists

jobs.why: shadcn for the base parts: buttons, dialogs, forms. The code is copied into my repo, so I own it.

feature.text: 21st.dev is where I look first for anything beyond the basics. It is a big community catalogue of React components. I search it like a shop, then install the one I pick with the shadcn command, so it lands in my repo like everything else. Search is free. Its AI generator needs a key and a paid plan.

alternatives.when: I want quiet motion built into the parts
it is a landing page and wants effects, like marquees and shiny borders
I want loud text and background effects
I want pieces with character, like a dynamic island
it is a dashboard and needs charts

jobs.why: Two agent skills with colour rules built in. They stop the agent picking the usual purple gradient.

alternatives.when: colours must look equally bright. OKLCH is a colour format that matches how eyes see lightness
I want to see how real products use colour first

jobs.why: Free fonts with real character, fine for commercial work.
jobs.note: No AI-default fonts: the few faces every AI tool reaches for. I pick one display face with character and one quiet text face.

jobs.job: I want references before I design
jobs.why: Real screens from real products, searchable by pattern.

alternatives.when: I want to sketch the layout on a canvas my agent can read

jobs.job: I want an agent to design with me
jobs.why: My own skill reads this toolkit and asks which tools fit. Context7 hands the agent current docs, so it doesn't guess old APIs.

alternatives.when: the interface exists and needs a critique and a polish
the first draft looks like a template
I want the official baseline skill
I want to see how a good skill is written

jobs.job: I want to prove it works
jobs.why: I capture frames about 1.5 seconds apart and compare them. A still screenshot never proves that something moves.

alternatives.when: I need the console, network or a performance trace
I want the page checked against a list of interface rules
